title: A Case of the Mondays: Shovels, Goalposts, and One Very Good Sandwich in the President's Box
paragraphs: Well, the Commanders went to Philadelphia and lost 24-22, which sounds like a normal football sentence until you remember this team spent all offseason promising us they were done with heartbreak. Instead, Washington gift-wrapped a fresh variety of it: a blocked extra point, a goalpost hug that cost them a shot to tie, and a failed two-point conversion that will live in DC infamy right next to every other cursed fourth-quarter decision this franchise has ever made. Jayden Daniels found Antonio Williams for a touchdown with 1:01 left to make it a two-point game, and for about ninety glorious seconds it felt like destiny. Then David Blough and Dan Quinn dialed up a shovel pass to tight end John Bates, Ojomo spun off Nick Allegretti like Allegretti wasn't there, and the dream died face down in the turf at the Linc.

Let's talk about Stefon Diggs, whose touchdown catch was so good he immediately ruined it by climbing the goalpost like he was trying to dunk on Lincoln Financial Field itself. The unsportsmanlike conduct flag pushed Washington back to a mere extra point instead of a two-point try, which, as Dan Quinn confirmed, they absolutely would have gone for otherwise. Diggs, to his credit, didn't try to spin it. "I take full accountability," he said, and Jayden Daniels backed him up with the understated line of the week: "We have to be smarter." Somewhere in the building, an entire offensive game plan quietly whispered, no kidding.

Quinn's postgame summary was the kind of thing you say when you've just watched your team lose a game it absolutely could have won: "That stings, man. A lot." He liked the fight, he liked the defense, he did not like the mistakes, and honestly neither did anyone else watching. The good news, and there is genuine good news, is that a defense many assumed would be a disaster area actually looked like it had teeth, holding a Jalen Hurts offense in check for long stretches before the big plays crept in late. Nicki Jhabvala noted the defense showed a real edge, and Amik Robertson put it about as well as anyone could: "We definitely have a special group... We just got to finish."

And then there's Tyler Owens, who did not throw a touchdown, did not make a tackle for a loss, and somehow became the single most talked-about Commander of Week 1 because of a punt coverage rep that made grown men on the internet lose their minds. John Keim called it one of the best special teams plays you'll see. His own teammates voted him the best athlete on the roster last year, and after Sunday it's not hard to see why. In a 24-22 loss that will otherwise be remembered for goalposts and shovel passes, Owens gave Commanders fans the one unambiguously fun thing to cling to, and lord knows they needed it.

Elsewhere in the NFL, Week 1 did what Week 1 always does, which is convince half the league's fan bases they're going to the Super Bowl and the other half that the sky is falling, all based on a single data point that means almost nothing by October. The Eagles, for their part, get to enjoy the smug satisfaction of a division win before Labor Day is even properly cold, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes NFC East football insufferable and also the only reason any of us watch it.

Now for the part of the column where I get to be smug for entirely different reasons. My wife works in the President's Box at UVA home games, which means on Saturday I was up there eating catered food and watching Virginia dismantle Norfolk State 59-3 at Scott Stadium while somewhere down the road in Philadelphia the Commanders were finding new ways to lose a two-point conversion. There is no better weekend in sports than one where your NFL team is losing on national television and your college team is busy putting up 59 points on a Saturday afternoon buffet you did not have to pay for.

Fifty-nine to three is not a game, it's a mismatch that got embarrassed by the scoreboard, and from where I was sitting it looked even more lopsided with a plate of catered chicken in one hand. Virginia didn't need any heroics, didn't need a shovel pass, didn't need anyone hugging a goalpost, they just showed up and scored touchdowns like it was a hobby. Next up for the Cavaliers is West Virginia, and if the President's Box menu is even half as good as it was this weekend, I will happily keep showing up to report on it, win or lose. The Commanders, meanwhile, will need a lot more than good snacks to fix what went wrong in Philadelphia, but hey, that's a problem for a different Monday, and probably several more after that.
